findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and can be bypassed
findings.body: `should_block?` uses `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` with the raw submitted value, and neither `BlockedEmail` nor `User` normalizes the address before validation. Since the domain part of an email is case-insensitive, a block for `spammer@gmail.com` will not match `spammer@Gmail.com`, allowing the same mailbox to sign up by changing the case of the domain or local part. The unique index does not help because it is also case-sensitive. Normalize addresses with `Email.downcase` before saving and querying blocked emails.

findings.title: BlockedEmail side effects run twice per signup
findings.body: `validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, which increments `match_count` and writes `last_match_at`. In `UsersController#create`, the same user record is validated first by `user.valid?` and then again by `user.save`, so a single signup attempt against a blocked or do_nothing email increments the counters twice. This makes the new match statistics inaccurate; the write should be removed from the validator or the controller should avoid the duplicate validation call.

findings.title: match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: `record.match_count += 1` followed by `record.save` loads the current count and writes the whole record. Two concurrent attempts for the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count`, and the last save will discard the other increment. Use `update_counters` or an SQL `match_count = match_count + 1` update if accurate statistics are required.
